title: Customs Duty and Tax Exemption Framework under Section 19
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of the legal basis for granting customs duty, VAT, and supplementary duty exemptions under Section 19 of the Customs Act, 1969. Over time, the legal framework shifted from referencing the VAT Act of 1991 to the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act of 2012, reflecting broader legislative updates in Bangladesh's tax regime.

evolution.legal_basis: Shifted from VAT Act 1991 to VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
evolution.scope: Expanded to include regulatory duties, advance tax, and income tax exemptions in specific SROs.

timeline.change: Initial framework referencing Customs Act 1969 and VAT Act 1991.
Transition to referencing VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 and Income-tax Ordinance 1984.
Formal legislative alignment updating references from VAT Act 1991 to VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

Customs Act 1969: Section 19 of this Act serves as the legal basis for the Government to grant exemptions from customs duties and other taxes.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides authority for the Government to grant exemptions from Value Added Tax on specific goods.
National Board of Revenue: The Government grants these specific tax exemptions in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
First Schedule: The goods eligible for exemption under this order are categorized within the First Schedule of the Customs Act 1969.
Poultry Farming Equipment: A wide range of machinery, parts, and specialized materials used in poultry farming are eligible for exemption from customs duty, value added tax, and supplementary duty. These items must be imported by poultry farms registered with the Board of Investment or the Department of Livestock Services. The exemption is conditional upon the items being installed or used exclusively at the registered farm premises, with a mandatory submission of a notarized bond and a post-installation verification report from the relevant industry association.

Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the government to grant exemptions from value added tax, advance tax, and supplementary duty.
Income-tax Ordinance 1984: Section 44(4)(b) of this Ordinance authorizes the government to grant exemptions from advance income tax.
National Board of Revenue: The government is required to consult with this body before exercising its power to grant duty and tax exemptions.
